question: What is the main smooth muscle that forms the wall of the urinary bladder?
explanation: The detrusor muscle is the primary smooth muscle of the bladder wall. It stretches as the bladder fills and contracts to push urine out during voiding. [learn more](BMP121_U3_T5#BMP121_U3_T5_h1)

question: Why does the detrusor muscle need to relax significantly while the bladder is storing urine?

options.A: To allow the bladder to hold urine without a high pressure increase
options.B: To push urine upward toward the kidneys continuously
options.C: To open the internal urethral sphincter automatically
options.D: To stimulate the pudendal nerve to close the external sphincter

explanation: Relaxing the detrusor muscle lets the bladder expand and hold more urine while keeping pressure low, which protects the upper urinary tract. [learn more](BMP121_U3_T5#BMP121_U3_T5_h1)

question: Which nerve pathway supplies the main signal for the bladder to contract when passing urine?
explanation: Parasympathetic fibers running through the pelvic splanchnic nerves stimulate the detrusor muscle to contract so the bladder can empty. [learn more](BMP121_U3_T5#BMP121_U3_T5_h2)

question: What is the main role of the sympathetic nervous system on the bladder while it is storing urine?

options.A: Sending pain signals directly to the cerebral cortex during filling
options.B: Triggering immediate bladder emptying when it reaches half capacity
options.C: Relaxing the external urethral sphincter to allow continuous dripping
options.D: Promoting urine retention by relaxing the detrusor and contracting the sphincter

explanation: Sympathetic activity takes over during the storage phase to keep the bladder relaxed and the internal sphincter firmly closed. [learn more](BMP121_U3_T5#BMP121_U3_T5_h2)

question: At about what volume does an adult bladder usually trigger the initial urge to pass urine?
explanation: The stretch receptors in a normal adult bladder trigger the micturition reflex when volume reaches about 300 to 400 mL. [learn more](BMP121_U3_T5#BMP121_U3_T5_h3)

question: Why do newborn babies wet themselves constantly without conscious control?

options.A: The micturition reflex is purely spinal and lacks adult higher brain modulation
options.B: The kidneys produce too much urine relative to body size
options.C: The external urethral sphincter is permanently paralyzed in infants
options.D: The detrusor muscle lacks the ability to contract on its own

explanation: Infant nervous systems are not yet fully matured, meaning the brain cannot yet override the basic spinal reflex that empties the bladder automatically. [learn more](BMP121_U3_T5#BMP121_U3_T5_h3)

question: Which specific part of the brainstem acts as the main coordination center for passing urine?
explanation: The pontine micturition center coordinates the relaxation of the sphincters and the contraction of the detrusor muscle for smooth urination. [learn more](BMP121_U3_T5#BMP121_U3_T5_h4)

question: A patient has a spinal cord injury above the sacral region but below the brainstem. What is the usual long-term bladder outcome?

options.A: Total permanent inability to ever produce urine
options.B: Complete lack of any bladder sensation or contraction forever
options.C: Normal voluntary control restored within a few days
options.D: Automatic reflex voiding without voluntary cerebral control

explanation: When brain control is blocked by a spinal injury, the lower spinal reflex arc remains intact, causing the bladder to empty automatically by reflex. [learn more](BMP121_U3_T5#BMP121_U3_T5_h4)

question: Which hormone is mainly responsible for relaxing the smooth muscle of the urinary tract during pregnancy?
explanation: Progesterone causes smooth muscles throughout the body to relax, which affects the ureters and bladder during pregnancy. [learn more](BMP121_U3_T5#BMP121_U3_T5_h5)

question: Why is a full bladder after childbirth a major concern for the midwife regarding postpartum hemorrhage?

options.A: Infection spreads rapidly to cause severe uterine atony
options.B: It causes immediate rupture of the external urethral sphincter
options.C: The retained urine directly dilutes circulating clotting factors
options.D: A full bladder displaces the uterus and prevents effective uterine contraction

explanation: A distended bladder pushes the uterus out of position, stopping it from contracting firmly to clamp down on blood vessels after delivery. [learn more](BMP121_U3_T5#BMP121_U3_T5_h5)
